# _autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md

# scribed.make_backend

Abstraction tools for *building* transcription facades.

Writing a new backend should be mostly declarative. This module supplies the
reusable machinery so an adapter is just “call the engine, return normalized
segments”:

- [`BaseTranscriberAdapter`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.BaseTranscriberAdapter) — subclass it and implement
  `_transcribe()`; kwarg translation (via the
  > backend’s `param_map`) is handled for you.
- [`make_segment()`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.make_segment) / [`make_word()`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.make_word) / [`normalize_confidence()`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.normalize_confidence) — build
  normalized [`Segment`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Segment) / [`Word`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Word) from
  whatever shape the engine returned, including confidence-scale normalization.
- [`scaffold_backend()`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.scaffold_backend) — generate a new `scribed/backends/<id>/` package
  from the template, pre-filled from the ledger entry. This is the one-command
  way to start a facade for any backend in the catalog.
- [`make_test_audio()`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.make_test_audio) / [`validate_adapter()`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.validate_adapter) — smoke-test an adapter end
  to end so you know a new facade actually wires up and returns the right type.

These are the “abstraction tools and skills that know the process” — the
companion `SKILL.md` walks an agent (or human) through using them.

### Functions

| [`make_segment`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.make_segment)(text, \*[, start, end, ...])          | Build a normalized [`Segment`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Segment).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_word`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.make_word)(text, \*[, start, end, confidence, ...]) | Build a normalized [`Word`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Word).         |
| [`normalize_confidence`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.normalize_confidence)(value, \*[, scale])           | Normalize a raw confidence to `[0, 1]` (dividing by `scale`).                                       |
| [`scaffold_backend`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.scaffold_backend)(backend_id, \*[, dest, ...])      | Create a new `scribed/backends/<id>/` package from the template.                                    |
| [`make_test_audio`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.make_test_audio)(\*[, duration, sample_rate, freq]) | Return WAV `bytes` of a short sine tone (needs numpy + soundfile).                                  |
| [`validate_adapter`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.validate_adapter)(backend_id, \*[, audio, ...])     | Smoke-test a backend adapter end to end, returning a report dict.                                   |

### Classes

| [`BaseTranscriberAdapter`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.BaseTranscriberAdapter)(config)   | Optional base class for backend adapters.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

### *class* scribed.make_backend.BaseTranscriberAdapter(config)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Optional base class for backend adapters.

Stores the config, builds a kwarg translator from `config['param_map']`,
and implements `transcribe` as: translate normalized kwargs -> native
kwargs -> `_transcribe()`. Subclasses implement `_transcribe()` and
return a [`Transcript`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Transcript).

Adapters are not *required* to subclass this — the registry only needs an
`Adapter` class with a `transcribe(audio, **kwargs)` method — but doing
so removes the boilerplate.

#### natively_streams *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)* *= False*

Override to `True` in a backend that talks a live protocol (WebSocket /
streaming recognizer) and implements `_stream_native()`. When `False`
(the default), live transcription is synthesized from batch `transcribe`.

#### *async* transcribe_live(source, , vad=None, \*\*kwargs)

Stream [`Segment`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Segment)s from a live `AudioSource`.

Native-streaming backends set [`natively_streams`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.BaseTranscriberAdapter.natively_streams) and override
`_stream_native()`; everyone else streams for free here via the
VAD-segmented batch fallback. `kwargs` flow to the per-utterance
`transcribe` (e.g. `language=`).

### scribed.make_backend.make_segment(text, , start=None, end=None, confidence=None, conf_scale=1.0, speaker=None, language=None, words=None, \*\*meta)

Build a normalized [`Segment`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Segment).

`start`/`end` are **seconds** (converted to the millisecond
[`TimeSpan`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.TimeSpan) internally). `confidence` is normalized to
`[0, 1]` via `conf_scale` (e.g. `conf_scale=100` for percent-scale
engines).

* **Return type:**
  [`Segment`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Segment)

### scribed.make_backend.make_test_audio(, duration=1.0, sample_rate=16000, freq=440.0)

Return WAV `bytes` of a short sine tone (needs numpy + soundfile).

A tone carries no speech, so it is a *wiring* smoke test: it proves an
adapter accepts audio, runs, and returns a [`Transcript`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Transcript)
of the right shape. To check actual recognition, pass a real speech clip to
[`validate_adapter()`](_autosummary/scribed.make_backend.html.md#scribed.make_backend.validate_adapter) via `audio=` together with `expect_text=`.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### scribed.make_backend.make_word(text, , start=None, end=None, confidence=None, conf_scale=1.0, speaker=None)

Build a normalized [`Word`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Word).

`start`/`end` are **seconds** (converted to the millisecond
[`TimeSpan`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.TimeSpan) internally). `confidence` is normalized to
`[0, 1]` via `conf_scale`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Word`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Word)

### scribed.make_backend.normalize_confidence(value, , scale=1.0)

Normalize a raw confidence to `[0, 1]` (dividing by `scale`).

`None` passes through. Use `scale=100` for engines that report `0..100`.
Engines that report a log-probability should convert before calling this.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### scribed.make_backend.scaffold_backend(backend_id, , dest=None, overwrite=False, ledger=None, extra_overrides=None)

Create a new `scribed/backends/<id>/` package from the template.

Pre-fills `config.py` from the backend’s ledger entry (if any) so you only
have to flesh out `param_map` and implement `adapter.py`’s
`_transcribe`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **backend_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The ledger id (e.g. `"deepgram"`, `"faster-whisper"`).
    The on-disk module name uses underscores; the config `id` keeps the
    id verbatim.
  * **dest** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – Target directory (defaults to `scribed/backends/<id_underscored>`).
  * **overwrite** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Allow writing into an existing non-empty directory.
  * **ledger** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – A [`Catalog`](_autosummary/scribed.html.md#scribed.Catalog) to read the record from
    (defaults to the shipped catalog).
  * **extra_overrides** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]) – Extra config-key overrides applied on top of the record.
* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)
* **Returns:**
  The path to the created backend package.

### scribed.make_backend.validate_adapter(backend_id, , audio=None, expect_text=None)

Smoke-test a backend adapter end to end, returning a report dict.

Loads the adapter (reporting unavailability instead of raising), runs
`transcribe` on a generated tone (or supplied `audio`), and checks the
contract: a [`Transcript`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Transcript) came back. Never raises on a
*recognition* mismatch — it returns what happened so callers can decide.

With a tone (no `audio`), `ok` means “ran and returned a Transcript”.
With `expect_text`, `ok` additionally requires the substring to appear.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md

# scribed.readers

Read a transcript back into a [`Transcript`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Transcript).

scribed writes subtitles (`Transcript.srt` / `.vtt`); this module is the
reading direction, for a transcript that already exists: an SRT or WebVTT from a
recording session, a Praat TextGrid from an aligner, a word-timed JSON from an
earlier ASR run, or plain `speaker: text` lines (untimed):

```default
t = scribed.read_transcript("take1.srt")      # or Transcript.parse(...)
for seg in t:
    print(seg.speaker, seg.start, seg.end, seg.words)
```

The format is detected by file suffix, then by content; pass `fmt` to force one
of [`FORMATS`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.FORMATS). A parsed transcript carries `backend="file:<fmt>"` so
downstream code can tell it from an ASR result. No dependencies.

```pycon
>>> t = read_transcript("1\n00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,500\n[carl] Hello there.\n")
>>> [(s.speaker, s.text, s.start, s.end) for s in t], t.backend
([('carl', 'Hello there.', 1.0, 2.5)], 'file:srt')
```

### Module Attributes

| [`FORMATS`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.FORMATS)   | The transcript formats read here, in detection order.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`detect_format`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.detect_format)(text, \*[, suffix])   | Which of [`FORMATS`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.FORMATS) `text` is: by file suffix first, then by content.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`parse_timestamp`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.parse_timestamp)(value)              | `HH:MM:SS,mmm` / `MM:SS.mmm` / plain seconds -> seconds.                                                              |
| [`read_transcript`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.read_transcript)(source, \*[, fmt])  | Read `source` (a path to a transcript file, or the transcript text itself).                                           |

### scribed.readers.FORMATS *: [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]* *= ('vtt', 'textgrid', 'json', 'srt', 'plain')*

The transcript formats read here, in detection order.

### scribed.readers.detect_format(text, , suffix='')

Which of [`FORMATS`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.FORMATS) `text` is: by file suffix first, then by content.

```pycon
>>> detect_format("WEBVTT\n\n00:01.000 --> 00:02.000\nhi")
'vtt'
>>> detect_format("1\n00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,000\nhi"), detect_format("hi there")
('srt', 'plain')
>>> detect_format('{"segments": []}'), detect_format("", suffix=".TextGrid")
('json', 'textgrid')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### scribed.readers.parse_timestamp(value)

`HH:MM:SS,mmm` / `MM:SS.mmm` / plain seconds -> seconds.

```pycon
>>> parse_timestamp("00:01:02,500"), parse_timestamp("01:02.5"), parse_timestamp("7.25")
(62.5, 62.5, 7.25)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### scribed.readers.read_transcript(source, , fmt=None)

Read `source` (a path to a transcript file, or the transcript text itself).

`fmt` (one of [`FORMATS`](_autosummary/scribed.readers.html.md#scribed.readers.FORMATS)) overrides detection. The result’s `backend`
is `"file:<fmt>"`.

```pycon
>>> t = read_transcript("carl: Hello.\nned: Hi.")
>>> t.speakers, t.backend, t.segments[0].span
(['carl', 'ned'], 'file:plain', None)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Transcript`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Transcript)


# _autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md

# scribed.registry

Backend discovery, registration, and lazy loading.

An *implemented* backend is a subpackage of [`scribed.backends`](_autosummary/scribed.backends.html.md#module-scribed.backends) that ships
two things:

- `config.py` defining a `BACKEND_CONFIG` dict (id, pip_install, capabilities,
  `param_map`, …), and
- `adapter.py` defining an `Adapter` class whose `transcribe(audio, **kwargs)`
  returns a [`scribed.base.Transcript`](_autosummary/scribed.base.html.md#scribed.base.Transcript).

This registry scans for those at first use, loads each adapter *lazily* (so
importing scribed never imports heavy engine SDKs), and raises a friendly
`pip install` error if a backend’s dependency is missing. Third parties can
register their own backends at runtime via [`register_backend()`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.register_backend).

The design mirrors the sibling `ocracy` facade, adapted for ASR: the primary
capability is `"transcribe"` (audio -> text+timing), with optional extra
capabilities (`"diarize"`, `"stream"`, `"translate"`, …) declared per
backend.

### Module Attributes

| [`PRIMARY_CAPABILITY`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.PRIMARY_CAPABILITY)   | The capability every general ASR backend provides.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`clear_registry`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.clear_registry)()                                | Clear all registered backends (useful for tests).                      |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`get_backend`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.get_backend)(backend_id)                         | Config + lazily-loaded adapter for a backend (raises on missing deps). |
| [`get_config`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.get_config)(backend_id)                          | A backend's `BACKEND_CONFIG` without loading its adapter.              |
| [`get_default_backend`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.get_default_backend)([capability, ...])          | Pick a sensible default backend id for a capability.                   |
| [`list_backends`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.list_backends)([capability])                     | Sorted ids of implemented backends, optionally filtered by capability. |
| [`register_backend`](_autosummary/scribed.registry.html.md#scribed.registry.register_backend)(backend_id, config[, adapter]) | Register a backend at runtime (for third-party plugins).               |

### scribed.registry.PRIMARY_CAPABILITY *= 'transcribe'*

The capability every general ASR backend provides.

### scribed.registry.clear_registry()

Clear all registered backends (useful for tests).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### scribed.registry.get_backend(backend_id)

Config + lazily-loaded adapter for a backend (raises on missing deps).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### scribed.registry.get_config(backend_id)

A backend’s `BACKEND_CONFIG` without loading its adapter.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### scribed.registry.get_default_backend(capability='transcribe', , require_available=True)

Pick a sensible default backend id for a capability.

Strategy (ASR-tuned): prefer a backend explicitly flagged `default_for` the
capability *and* whose dependency is importable; then any importable backend
for the capability; then — if `require_available` is False or nothing is
installed — the first registered candidate (using it will raise a helpful
install error).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### scribed.registry.list_backends(capability=None)

Sorted ids of implemented backends, optionally filtered by capability.

A backend matches `capability` if it appears in the backend’s
`capabilities` list (the primary `"transcribe"` is implied for all).

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### scribed.registry.register_backend(backend_id, config, adapter=None)

Register a backend at runtime (for third-party plugins).

* **Parameters:**
  * **backend_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Unique identifier.
  * **config** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – `BACKEND_CONFIG`-shaped dict (needs at least `name`).
  * **adapter** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – Optional pre-instantiated adapter; else loaded lazily from
    `config['module_path']` when first used.
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/scribed.status.html.md

# scribed.status

Backend readiness status — four nested levels, info dicts, and a Markdown table.

scribed describes far more ASR engines than any one machine has ready to run, so
it helps to know, at a glance, where each one stands. Four **nested** levels:

1. **all** — every engine in the ledger (`scribed/data/backends.json`).
2. **implemented** — scribed ships a working facade for it (`⊆ all`).
3. **set_up** — ready to run *here, now*: the engine/client library is importable
   and, for a remote backend, its credential env var is present (`⊆ implemented`).
4. **tested** — actually produced a transcript from a tone clip on this machine
   (`⊆ set_up`).

`all ⊇ implemented ⊇ set_up ⊇ tested`.

API:

- [`backend_ids()`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.backend_ids) — the id list at a level.
- [`backend_info()`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.backend_info) — `{id: {...all ledger fields..., implemented, set_up, tested}}`.
- [`status_table()`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.status_table) — an aligned Markdown table (also readable as plain text).
- [`names_with_sites()`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.names_with_sites) — `"Name (website), ..."` for a set of ids.

#### NOTE
computing **tested** runs real transcription — for *remote* backends that
means a real (possibly billed) API call. Use the `run_tests` argument to
control exactly which backends get called.

### Functions

| [`is_set_up`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.is_set_up)(backend_id)                      | Ready to run here & now.                                                              |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`is_tested`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.is_tested)(backend_id, \*[, audio])         | Actually run transcription on `audio` (a generated tone if None); True iff it worked. |
| [`backend_ids`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.backend_ids)([level, info, test_audio])     | Sorted backend ids at a readiness `level` (one of `LEVELS`).                          |
| [`backend_info`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.backend_info)([ids, run_tests, test_audio]) | Per-backend status: every ledger field plus `implemented`/`set_up`/`tested`.          |
| [`status_table`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.status_table)([ids, info, columns, ...])    | Render an aligned Markdown table of backend status (also plain-text readable).        |
| [`names_with_sites`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.names_with_sites)(ids, \*[, info])          | `"Name (website), Name2 (website2), ..."` for `ids` (name, not id).                   |

### scribed.status.backend_ids(level='all', , info=None, test_audio=None)

Sorted backend ids at a readiness `level` (one of `LEVELS`).

Pass a precomputed `info` (from [`backend_info()`](_autosummary/scribed.status.html.md#scribed.status.backend_info)) to avoid recomputation
— important for `"tested"`, which otherwise re-runs transcription.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### scribed.status.backend_info(ids=None, , run_tests=False, test_audio=None)

Per-backend status: every ledger field plus `implemented`/`set_up`/`tested`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **ids** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – Which backends (default: every ledger id).
  * **run_tests** – Which set-up backends to actually transcription-test. `True` =
    all set-up (real API calls for remotes!); `False` = none (`tested`
    is `None`); or an iterable of ids to limit testing to those.
  * **test_audio** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – Audio to test with (default: a generated tone, shared across all).
* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]
* **Returns:**
  `{id: {..., "name", "website", "implemented", "set_up", "tested"}}` where
  `tested` is `True`/`False`/`None` (None = not attempted).

### scribed.status.is_set_up(backend_id)

Ready to run here & now.

Requires the engine/client to be importable (local *and* remote), and — for a
remote backend — its (primary) credential env var to resolve. So a remote
whose key is set but whose client library isn’t installed is *not* set up
(it couldn’t actually run). Returns False for ledger-only backends.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### scribed.status.is_tested(backend_id, , audio=None)

Actually run transcription on `audio` (a generated tone if None); True iff it worked.

For remote backends this performs a real API call. Returns False if the
backend isn’t set up or the run fails.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### scribed.status.names_with_sites(ids, , info=None)

`"Name (website), Name2 (website2), ..."` for `ids` (name, not id).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### scribed.status.status_table(ids=None, , info=None, columns=None, run_tests=False, test_audio=None)

Render an aligned Markdown table of backend status (also plain-text readable).

Rows are ordered tested → set-up → implemented → listed, then by name, so the
“live” backends float to the top. Pass a precomputed `info` to avoid re-running
tests; otherwise `run_tests` controls which set-up backends get tested.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/scribed.tools.html.md

# scribed.tools

Command-line tools for scribed (dispatched via `cw` in `__main__`).

Each function here is a thin, CLI-friendly wrapper over the Python API; `cw`
turns their signatures into subcommands and options. Run `scribed <command>
--help` (after `pip install 'scribed[cli]'`) or `python -m scribed <command>`.

### Functions

| [`transcribe`](_autosummary/scribed.tools.html.md#scribed.tools.transcribe)(audio, \*[, backend, language, ...])   | Transcribe an audio file/URL and print the result.                                  |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`backends`](_autosummary/scribed.tools.html.md#scribed.tools.backends)(\*[, capability])                        | List the backends scribed can run right now (optionally by capability).             |

# _autosummary/scribed.translation.html.md

# scribed.translation

Parameter translation between scribed’s normalized kwargs and native engines.

Every backend exposes its own parameter names and scales (`language` vs
`lang` vs `language_code`; `diarize` vs `speaker_labels`;
`timestamps='word'` vs `word_timestamps=True`). A backend declares a
`param_map` in its `BACKEND_CONFIG` mapping *normalized* names to native
ones, and [`make_kwargs_translator()`](_autosummary/scribed.translation.html.md#scribed.translation.make_kwargs_translator) turns that declaration into a function
that rewrites caller kwargs into the shape the engine wants. This keeps the
facade’s vocabulary stable while letting each adapter stay a thin shim.

This mirrors the translation layer used by the sibling `ocracy` facade so the
two packages feel the same to read and extend.

### Functions

| [`make_kwargs_translator`](_autosummary/scribed.translation.html.md#scribed.translation.make_kwargs_translator)(param_map, \*[, ...])   | Create a function that translates normalized kwargs to native kwargs.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`validate_param`](_autosummary/scribed.translation.html.md#scribed.translation.validate_param)(name, value, config)            | Validate a single parameter against `min`/`max`/`choices` in config.    |

### scribed.translation.make_kwargs_translator(param_map, , on_unsupported='warn')

Create a function that translates normalized kwargs to native kwargs.

* **Parameters:**
  * **param_map** ([`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]) – 

    Mapping of `normalized_name -> native config dict` where the
    config dict may have:
    - `native_name` (str): the backend’s parameter name (defaults to
      the normalized name).
    - `coerce` (callable): transform the value (e.g. a bool -> the
      string a vendor expects, `["en"] -> "en"`).
    - `default` (Any): value to inject when the caller omits the param.
    - `None` as the whole value: the parameter is explicitly *not*
      supported by this backend.
  * **on_unsupported** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What to do with caller params absent from `param_map`:
    `"warn"` (default), `"raise"`, or `"ignore"`.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]
* **Returns:**
  A `translate(**kwargs) -> dict` function.

### scribed.translation.validate_param(name, value, config)

Validate a single parameter against `min`/`max`/`choices` in config.

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)


# _autosummary/scribed.util.html.md

# scribed.util

Audio-input normalization and small shared helpers.

Different ASR backends want their input in different forms: a filesystem path
(local Whisper, faster-whisper — they shell out to ffmpeg), raw `bytes` or a
file object (most cloud REST APIs), or a numpy waveform (deep-learning engines).
Callers, meanwhile, want to pass whatever they have — a path, an `http(s)` URL,
bytes, a file-like object, or a numpy array. This module bridges the two with a
handful of converters that **lazily** import soundfile / numpy / urllib only when
actually exercised, so `import scribed` stays dependency-free.

The key converters:

- [`load_audio_bytes()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.load_audio_bytes) — anything -> encoded audio `bytes` (for REST APIs).
- [`ensure_file_path()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.ensure_file_path) — anything -> a path on disk (writing a temp file for
  in-memory inputs); pair with [`cleanup_temp()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.cleanup_temp) or use [`audio_path()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.audio_path).
- [`audio_path()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.audio_path) — a context manager yielding a path and cleaning up.
- [`to_waveform()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.to_waveform) — anything -> `(numpy float32 mono, sample_rate)`.

### Functions

| [`classify_input`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.classify_input)(audio)                              | Classify an audio input as `url`/`path`/`bytes`/`file`/`numpy`.                                                         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`is_url`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.is_url)(x)                                          | True if `x` is a string that looks like an http(s) URL.                                                                 |
| [`load_audio_bytes`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.load_audio_bytes)(audio, \*[, sample_rate])         | Return encoded audio `bytes` for any supported input.                                                                   |
| [`ensure_file_path`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.ensure_file_path)(audio, \*[, suffix, sample_rate]) | Return `(path, is_temp)` for any supported input.                                                                       |
| [`cleanup_temp`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.cleanup_temp)(path, is_temp)                        | Delete `path` iff `is_temp` (the flag returned by [`ensure_file_path()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.ensure_file_path)). |
| [`audio_path`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.audio_path)(audio, \*[, suffix])                    | Context manager yielding a filesystem path for `audio`, cleaning up temps.                                              |
| [`to_waveform`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.to_waveform)(audio, \*[, sample_rate])              | Convert any supported input into `(numpy float32 mono, sample_rate)`.                                                   |
| [`check_import`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.check_import)(module_name, \*, install_hint[, ...]) | Import `module_name` or raise a friendly, actionable ImportError.                                                       |

### scribed.util.audio_path(audio, , suffix='.wav')

Context manager yielding a filesystem path for `audio`, cleaning up temps.

Example:

```default
with audio_path(raw_bytes) as p:
    segments = model.transcribe(p)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### scribed.util.check_import(module_name, , install_hint, feature='this')

Import `module_name` or raise a friendly, actionable ImportError.

Centralizes the “you need to `pip install X`” guidance so adapters and
converters don’t each hand-roll it.

### scribed.util.classify_input(audio)

Classify an audio input as `url`/`path`/`bytes`/`file`/`numpy`.

Decided structurally (and via duck typing for file objects / numpy) so we
never import soundfile or numpy just to look at the input.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### scribed.util.cleanup_temp(path, is_temp)

Delete `path` iff `is_temp` (the flag returned by [`ensure_file_path()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.ensure_file_path)).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### scribed.util.ensure_file_path(audio, , suffix='.wav', sample_rate=16000)

Return `(path, is_temp)` for any supported input.

Existing on-disk paths are returned untouched (`is_temp=False`). In-memory
inputs (bytes/URL/file/numpy) are written to a temp file (`is_temp=True`);
the caller is responsible for cleanup (use [`cleanup_temp()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.cleanup_temp), or prefer
the [`audio_path()`](_autosummary/scribed.util.html.md#scribed.util.audio_path) context manager).

* **Return type:**
  [`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]

### scribed.util.is_url(x)

True if `x` is a string that looks like an http(s) URL.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### scribed.util.load_audio_bytes(audio, , sample_rate=16000)

Return encoded audio `bytes` for any supported input.

Pass-through for `bytes`; reads files and file objects; fetches URLs;
encodes numpy waveforms as WAV (at `sample_rate`).

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### scribed.util.to_waveform(audio, , sample_rate=16000)

Convert any supported input into `(numpy float32 mono, sample_rate)`.

Numpy input is returned as-is (paired with `sample_rate`). Everything else
is decoded with soundfile and resampled is *not* performed — the returned
sample rate is whatever the source had (numpy inputs excepted).

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`scribed` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `scribed`

Transcribe audio to text through one façade over many speech-to-text (ASR) engines — local (Whisper, faster-whisper, whisper.cpp, Vosk) and cloud (OpenAI, Groq, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Google, ElevenLabs). Use when the user wants to transcribe speech/audio/a recording/a podcast/a meeting/a voice memo to text, get subtitles (SRT/VTT), diarize speakers, or choose between transcription engines. Triggers on “transcribe”, “speech to text”, “audio to text”, “get subtitles”, “who said what”, “diarize”.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/scribed scribed --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`scribed/data/skills/scribed`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/scribed/tree/HEAD/scribed/data/skills/scribed) (bundled with the pip package).

### `scribed-add-backend`

Add a new speech-to-text engine to scribed by writing a backend façade (config.py + adapter.py) that normalizes the engine into scribed’s Transcript. Use when the user wants to wrap/support a transcription engine scribed doesn’t implement yet (e.g. Speechmatics, NVIDIA Parakeet, AWS Transcribe, Azure Speech, a custom/in-house ASR), asks “how do I add a backend to scribed”, or wants to scaffold/implement a new adapter.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/scribed scribed-add-backend --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`scribed/data/skills/scribed-add-backend`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/scribed/tree/HEAD/scribed/data/skills/scribed-add-backend) (bundled with the pip package).

### `scribed-choose-backend`

Choose the right speech-to-text engine for a transcription job using scribed’s ledger — weigh local-vs-cloud, cost, speed, diarization, streaming, word timestamps, and language coverage. Use when the user asks “which transcription engine should I use”, “what’s the cheapest/fastest/most accurate STT”, “do I need a cloud API or can I run it locally”, “which one does speaker diarization”, or wants to compare ASR options.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/scribed scribed-choose-backend --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`scribed/data/skills/scribed-choose-backend`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/scribed/tree/HEAD/scribed/data/skills/scribed-choose-backend) (bundled with the pip package).

### `scribed-install-backend`

Get a scribed speech-to-text backend actually running — resolve its pip extra, system dependencies (e.g. ffmpeg), GPU wheels, first-run model weights, and API credentials. Use when transcription fails with a missing-dependency or missing-credential error, when the user asks “how do I install/set up <engine>”, “scribed says backend not available”, “ffmpeg not found”, or “where do I get a Deepgram/AssemblyAI/OpenAI key”.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/scribed scribed-install-backend --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`scribed/data/skills/scribed-install-backend`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/scribed/tree/HEAD/scribed/data/skills/scribed-install-backend) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install scribed`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/scribed/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`scribed.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/scribed/scribed.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/scribed/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)


# api.html.md

# API reference

| [`scribed`](_autosummary/scribed.html.md#module-scribed)   | scribed — one facade over many speech-to-text engines, plus a ledger to choose.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
